cat >> app/services/users.py <<EOF

def create_user(name: str, email: str) -> dict | None:
    # Check if email exists
    if store.find_by_email(email.lower()):
        return None
    
    # Calculate next id
    new_id = max(_USERS.keys()) + 1 if _USERS else 1
    
    new_user = {"id": new_id, "name": name, "email": email}
    _USERS[new_id] = new_user
    return new_user
EOF

from app.api.handlers import handle_create_user, handle_get_user

def test_create_user_ok():
    status, user = handle_create_user({"name": "Bob", "email": "bob@example.com"})
    assert status == 201
    assert user["name"] == "Bob"
    assert user["email"] == "bob@example.com"
    assert "id" in user
    
    # Verify retrieval
    status, retrieved = handle_get_user({"id": str(user["id"])})
    assert status == 200
    assert retrieved == user

def test_create_user_invalid_name():
    assert handle_create_user({"name": "", "email": "a@b.com"})[0] == 400
    assert handle_create_user({"name": "   ", "email": "a@b.com"})[0] == 400

def test_create_user_invalid_email():
    assert handle_create_user({"name": "Bob", "email": "invalid"})[0] == 400

def test_create_user_duplicate_email():
    handle_create_user({"name": "Bob", "email": "bob@example.com"})
    status, response = handle_create_user({"name": "Bob2", "email": "BOB@example.com"})
    assert status == 409
    assert response["error"] == "email already exists"
